en.title: 🔥 No modeling, no artists: one person used AI to build a full-fledged 3D action game that's genuinely playable—and released the full prompt set, from single-image rigging to a two-platform playable demo
en.summary:
🔥 No modeling skills, no artist needed! One person builds a genuinely hard-hitting 3D action game with AI — the full prompt set is public, from rigging a single image to a playable demo on both PC and mobile

Fini.Yang · X · @FiniYang · 2026-11-23 11:37
📌 This article is a repost; copyright belongs to the original author. Refer to the original link for the full text.

This piece breaks down the entire workflow — from building 3D out of a single image, to curing clipping and foot sliding, to delivering real hit feedback — complete with 9 tested prompts, a lossless asset-slimming script, an anti-foot-slide formula, and a 6-gate AI master control prompt. Even if you've never touched Blender, you can follow along and end up with something playable on both PC and mobile.

Plenty of people who play games and have tried their hand at AI 3D projects hit the same wall: getting a little character to move on screen takes one evening, but the moment you put a spear in its hands and have it lunge forward, it almost always goes full glitch — the cape on its back gets stretched by a thigh into a hammock 30 times its length, the feet spin in place like they're on ice, and the two hands swing independently, unable to grip the shaft.

Making a cube hop around is too easy to be interesting, so for the past two weeks I ran the whole pipeline for real on the most glitch-prone project I could pick, *Dark Three Kingdoms: Lone Spear Into the Night*: Zhao Yun rides alone, cutting his way out of a desolate village…

en.title: Pinterest replaced multi-stage clustering with LLMs, but the biggest speedup came from less reasoning
en.summary:
Pinterest replaces user journey clustering with 4-billion-parameter Qwen3 model, says engagement metrics improved.

Length: 1,222 characters
Reading time: about 4 minutes

Pinterest replaced its multi-stage clustering pipeline with a fine-tuned 4-billion-parameter language model, modeling user journey inference as a generation task and significantly improving email click-through rate (+1.1%) and push open rate (+1.3%).

A journey is defined as a behavior sequence across sessions that coherently reflects goals, intent, and context. The model’s input includes 150 temporal behaviors and a lightweight profile, and it generates prioritized journey names weighted by repetitiveness, recency, and specificity. The old clustering approach tended to fragment related behaviors, produce generic labels, and misclassify incidental interactions.

Intended for recommender systems engineers, AI product leads, and growth algorithm engineers.

Pinterest has moved its user journey inference system from a multi-stage clustering pipeline to a fine-tuned 4-billion-parameter language model, reporting a 1.1% lift in email click-through rate and a 1.3% lift in push notification open rate.

Instead of clustering keywords into interests, the model analyzes user activity history, identifies long-term goals, and feeds those journeys into Pinterest’s existing recommendation infrastructure.

Pinterest defines a journey as spanning multiple sessions and connecting interests...
en.reason: Pinterest replaced its multi-stage user-journey clustering pipeline with a fine-tuned 4-billion-parameter Qwen3 model, lifting email click-through by 1.1% and push open rates by 1.3%, with its biggest speedup coming from skipping recently processed users and doing less inference.

en.title: Learning Agent now is like getting into Douyin in 2018. If you had started learning self-media in 2020, you would surely have built up solid results by now; the same goes for starting to learn AI Agent development now. Back then, no one realized that self-media meant a disruption to content distribution: gaining hundreds or thousands of followers was no longer a privilege reserved for celebrities, and promoting a product no longer necessarily meant working with traditional media.

en.title: 🔥 No modeling, no artists: one person used AI to build a full-fledged 3D action game that's genuinely playable—and released the full prompt set, from single-image rigging to a two-platform playable demo
en.summary:
🔥 No modeling skills, no artist needed! One person builds a genuinely hard-hitting 3D action game with AI — the full prompt set is public, from rigging a single image to a playable demo on both PC and mobile

Fini.Yang · X · @FiniYang · 2026-11-23 11:37
📌 This article is a repost; copyright belongs to the original author. Refer to the original link for the full text.

This piece breaks down the entire workflow — from building 3D out of a single image, to curing clipping and foot sliding, to delivering real hit feedback — complete with 9 tested prompts, a lossless asset-slimming script, an anti-foot-slide formula, and a 6-gate AI master control prompt. Even if you've never touched Blender, you can follow along and end up with something playable on both PC and mobile.

Plenty of people who play games and have tried their hand at AI 3D projects hit the same wall: getting a little character to move on screen takes one evening, but the moment you put a spear in its hands and have it lunge forward, it almost always goes full glitch — the cape on its back gets stretched by a thigh into a hammock 30 times its length, the feet spin in place like they're on ice, and the two hands swing independently, unable to grip the shaft.

Making a cube hop around is too easy to be interesting, so for the past two weeks I ran the whole pipeline for real on the most glitch-prone project I could pick, *Dark Three Kingdoms: Lone Spear Into the Night*: Zhao Yun rides alone, cutting his way out of a desolate village…

en.title: Pinterest replaced multi-stage clustering with LLMs, but the biggest speedup came from less reasoning
en.summary:
Pinterest replaces user journey clustering with 4-billion-parameter Qwen3 model, says engagement metrics improved.

Length: 1,222 characters
Reading time: about 4 minutes

Pinterest replaced its multi-stage clustering pipeline with a fine-tuned 4-billion-parameter language model, modeling user journey inference as a generation task and significantly improving email click-through rate (+1.1%) and push open rate (+1.3%).

A journey is defined as a behavior sequence across sessions that coherently reflects goals, intent, and context. The model’s input includes 150 temporal behaviors and a lightweight profile, and it generates prioritized journey names weighted by repetitiveness, recency, and specificity. The old clustering approach tended to fragment related behaviors, produce generic labels, and misclassify incidental interactions.

Intended for recommender systems engineers, AI product leads, and growth algorithm engineers.

Pinterest has moved its user journey inference system from a multi-stage clustering pipeline to a fine-tuned 4-billion-parameter language model, reporting a 1.1% lift in email click-through rate and a 1.3% lift in push notification open rate.

Instead of clustering keywords into interests, the model analyzes user activity history, identifies long-term goals, and feeds those journeys into Pinterest’s existing recommendation infrastructure.

Pinterest defines a journey as spanning multiple sessions and connecting interests...
en.reason: Pinterest replaced its multi-stage user-journey clustering pipeline with a fine-tuned 4-billion-parameter Qwen3 model, lifting email click-through by 1.1% and push open rates by 1.3%, with its biggest speedup coming from skipping recently processed users and doing less inference.
